history.heading: Ancient peoples and kingdoms
paragraphs: South Africa has some of the world's oldest evidence of human ancestors, at the Cradle of Humankind sites, and of modern human behaviour, such as Blombos Cave. San and Khoikhoi peoples lived across the region for thousands of years. Bantu-speaking farmers arrived from the north, and the kingdom of Mapungubwe flourished around 1200 CE.

history.heading: Colonial era
paragraphs: The Dutch East India Company founded Cape Town in 1652 as a supply station. Dutch settlers (later called Boers or Afrikaners) expanded inland, displacing Khoikhoi and San peoples and using enslaved people from Asia and Africa. Britain took the Cape in 1806. Boers moved inland in the Great Trek and founded republics. The Zulu Kingdom under Shaka became a major power.

The discovery of diamonds (1867) and gold (1886) transformed the region. Britain defeated the Zulu in 1879 and the Boer republics in the Anglo-Boer War (1899–1902). The Union of South Africa was created in 1910.

history.heading: Apartheid
paragraphs: From 1948 the National Party imposed apartheid, a system of racial segregation and white minority rule. Black South Africans were stripped of rights and forced into "homelands". The African National Congress (ANC) and others resisted; the Sharpeville massacre in 1960 and the Soweto uprising in 1976 drew world attention. Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 27 years.

International sanctions and internal resistance led President F. W. de Klerk to release Mandela in 1990. The first democratic elections were held in 1994, and Mandela became president. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission investigated apartheid-era crimes.

history.heading: Democratic South Africa
paragraphs: The ANC dominated politics after 1994. Jacob Zuma's presidency (2009–2018) was marked by "state capture" corruption. In the 2024 election, the ANC lost its majority for the first time and formed a Government of National Unity with the Democratic Alliance and others. South Africa hosted the G20 summit in 2025.

culture.heading: The Rainbow Nation
paragraphs: South Africa has 12 official languages, including Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, English, Sesotho and South African Sign Language. Its diverse population includes Black Africans (about 80 percent), coloured, white and Indian South Africans. Most people are Christian.

Writers Nadine Gordimer and J. M. Coetzee won the Nobel Prize in Literature. Music ranges from mbaqanga and isicathamiya (Ladysmith Black Mambazo) to kwaito and amapiano, a globally popular genre. Braai (barbecue), bobotie and biltong are favourite foods.

culture.heading: Sport
paragraphs: Rugby, football and cricket are major sports. The Springboks' 1995 Rugby World Cup victory, with Mandela wearing the team's jersey, became a symbol of reconciliation, and they have won the tournament a record four times. South Africa hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: South Africa is a parliamentary republic in which the National Assembly elects the president. It has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial). The 1996 constitution is widely admired for its bill of rights. Challenges include corruption, crime, inequality, and failing public services in some municipalities.
South Africa is a member of BRICS and the G20 and brought a genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice in 2023. Relations with the United States became strained in 2025.

economy.heading: Africa's most industrialised economy
paragraphs: South Africa has the most industrialised and diversified economy in Africa. It is a leading producer of platinum, gold, chromium, manganese and coal, and has strong financial, manufacturing (cars), agricultural and tourism sectors. Johannesburg hosts Africa's largest stock exchange.

Growth has been weak for over a decade. Unemployment is among the highest in the world, around a third of the workforce, and inequality is extreme. Electricity shortages (load-shedding) and problems with ports and railways hampered the economy, though power cuts eased in 2024. The currency is the rand.
